adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the previously-used DuckDB implementation (`github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`) with a new `pkg/expr/sql` `DB` whose methods `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` all return `errors.New("not implemented")` (new file `pkg/expr/sql/db.go`). Call sites were updated to use this replacement (e.g., `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands`, and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto`), which will now fail at runtime. Additionally, `ReadQuery` for `QueryTypeSQL` is now unconditionally blocked because `enableSqlExpressions` always returns `false`, so SQL expressions error out for everyone. This is a real regression in behavior introduced by the diff.

Yet the diff contains no added/updated test files (no `*_test.go` changes) or other verification. While the claim about “P0 regressions reaching production” is speculative, the core point—behavior changes without accompanying tests/verification—is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error string 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' in pkg/expr/reader.go:130-131 conflates the flag gate with the missing implementation, making the user-facing contract ambiguous

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the QueryTypeSQL gate returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when `enableSqlExpressions(h)` is false. From the diff, this false case represents feature gating (based on `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`), so the user-facing error message indeed conflates “feature disabled” with “missing implementation,” making the contract ambiguous as the finding states.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() returns false in all paths: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false both in the `if enabled { ... }` branch and at the end. As a result, ReadQuery’s QueryTypeSQL case always hits `if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }`, so FlagSqlExpressions has no effect and SQL expressions are unconditionally disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL expression path returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' unconditionally, hard-failing queries even for users with the feature flag enabled

Therefore SQL queries will always hard-fail with `sqlExpressions is not implemented`, even when featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Replacement DB implementation is an empty struct with all methods returning 'not implemented' while the working go-duck dependency is removed, breaking SQL expression execution

Call sites were updated to use this stub (`duck.NewInMemoryDB()` -> `NewInMemoryDB()` in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go; and `QueryFramesInto` via `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` in pkg/expr/sql_command.go), which would make SQL execution fail if reached. If no `sql` import already exists in the file (not shown in the diff), this will not compile due to an undefined `sql` identifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gating error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is user-facing text that misleads users with the flag enabled and duplicates gate state that must be updated in two places

adjudication.rationale:
In `pkg/expr/reader.go`, the new gate `enableSqlExpressions(h)` is intended to depend on `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, but the implementation always returns `false`:

```go
enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
if enabled { return false }
return false
```

As a result, `ReadQuery` will *always* return `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` for `QueryTypeSQL`, even when the feature flag is enabled. This is a verifiable behavior defect introduced by the diff; the finding’s “misleads users with the flag enabled” aspect follows directly from this always-false gate.

As a result, ReadQuery’s QueryTypeSQL path always errors (`return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`), making SQL expressions unreachable and effectively ignoring FlagSqlExpressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stub interface shape (TablesList(rawSQL string), QueryFramesInto with frames and no DB handle) bakes in the old in-memory-duck assumption, making a real implementation riskier to change

Call sites (e.g., `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go`) hardcode `NewInMemoryDB()` rather than accepting an injected DB/engine, which does implicitly preserve an in-memory-only assumption and could make a future real implementation/API refactor more invasive. adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL string interpolation with inadequate escaping in parser.go:23: user-supplied SQL is spliced into a string literal protected only by doubling single quotes, allowing injection breakout once RunCommands is implemented

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, rawSQL is interpolated into a single-quoted SQL string literal after replacing `'` with `''`, which is the standard way to prevent breaking out of a SQL string literal. Additionally, in this diff the underlying DB implementation is a stub (pkg/expr/sql/db.go RunCommands returns "not implemented"), and SQL expressions are effectively disabled (enableSqlExpressions always returns false, causing QueryTypeSQL to return an error). The finding asserts an injection breakout enabled by this diff, but the diff does not show executable SQL command handling where such an injection would be realizable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RunCommands([]string) API shape institutionalizes raw command execution, taking pre-built SQL strings instead of a parsed query/AST plus parameters, inviting injection at every future call site

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new in-memory SQL DB wrapper with a `RunCommands(commands []string)` method that accepts prebuilt SQL strings (`pkg/expr/sql/db.go`). It is then used by `TablesList` to execute a formatted SQL command built via `fmt.Sprintf(...)` (`pkg/expr/sql/parser.go`). This does indeed cement an API that encourages raw-string SQL execution rather than structured/parameterized queries. However, the specific “inviting injection at every future call site” claim is forward-looking/speculative, and the current call site attempts basic escaping (`strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)`), so it’s not a directly verifiable security defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:128-132 — the QueryTypeSQL rejection occurs before iter.ReadVal(q), making the SQLExpression struct decode added at this site untestable dead code with zero coverage of the decode-and-validate sequence (getReferenceVar, refID validation) on the enable path

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go the new guard in the QueryTypeSQL case returns early when `!enabled`. The added `enableSqlExpressions` helper always returns false (`return false` in all branches), so the function will always reject SQL queries before `iter.ReadVal(q)` is reached. This makes the SQLExpression decoding/validation path unreachable (dead code) and breaks SQL query handling entirely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches (pkg/expr/reader.go:194-199), so QueryTypeSQL always returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then returns false in both the `if enabled { ... }` branch and the final return, so it can never return true. Since ReadQuery() for QueryTypeSQL now errors when `!enabled`, SQL queries will always return `sqlExpressions is not implemented` regardless of feature flags.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go replaces the real DuckDB implementation with stubs that always error, causing TablesList and SQLCommand.Execute to fail at runtime for every SQL expression, a functional regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior DuckDB-backed implementation (go-duck import and duck.NewInMemoryDB usage) and replaces it with pkg/expr/sql/db.go where DB.RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList all return "not implemented" errors. parser.go now calls NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, so TablesList will error if invoked. sql_command.go now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto, which will also always error if reached. Additionally, enableSqlExpressions() in reader.go always returns false, making SQL expressions unusable. This is a concrete behavior break/regression from the previous real implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:193–199 enableSqlExpressions can never return true because every branch returns false, so SQL expressions are dead regardless of the flag and QueryTypeSQL requests always return 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions always returns false: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false both in the `if enabled` branch and after it. Therefore `enabled := enableSqlExpressions(h)` is always false, and the QueryTypeSQL path always returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` regardless of the feature flag state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:9–23 DB implementation is a stub where every method returns errors.New('not implemented'), so every SQL expression command fails at runtime with a generic error

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds pkg/expr/sql/db.go where DB.TablesList/RunCommands/QueryFramesInto all return errors.New("not implemented"). The existing code is rewired to use this stub: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go now calls NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...) and pkg/expr/sql_command.go now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...). Those call paths will deterministically fail with the generic "not implemented" error if reached, breaking SQL expression parsing/execution behavior compared to the previous duck.NewInMemoryDB() implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql_command.go Execute → db.QueryFramesInto fails on every SQL expression command, surfacing 'not implemented' as rsp.Error (sql_command.go:100–104)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces pkg/expr/sql/db.go where DB.QueryFramesInto unconditionally returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. In pkg/expr/sql_command.go, Execute now constructs `db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` and calls `db.QueryFramesInto(...)`, so if Execute is reached it will always set `rsp.Error` to that not-implemented error. This broken behavior is directly verifiable from the added stub implementation and the updated call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parser.go:23–25 TablesList → RunCommands returns 'not implemented', so any code path inspecting table references in SQL expressions fails on every call

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now constructs duckDB := NewInMemoryDB() (previously duck.NewInMemoryDB()). The new implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go defines DB.RunCommands(...) to always return an error "not implemented". Since TablesList unconditionally calls duckDB.RunCommands([]string{cmd}), it will fail on every invocation, breaking any path that relies on SQL table inspection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No telemetry distinguishes 'feature disabled' from 'backend missing', making the guaranteed-failing deployment hard to diagnose

adjudication.rationale: From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that there is “no telemetry” distinguishing the cases, and the code paths shown would at least produce different observable errors: feature-gated failure returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` in `ReadQuery`, while a missing/unimplemented backend would return `errors.New("not implemented")` from `QueryFramesInto` and gets logged in `SQLCommand.Execute` (`logger.Error("Failed to query frames", ...)`). Also, the diff doesn’t show any explicit “backend missing” detection—only stubs—so the claimed distinction is speculative beyond what’s in the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96–104 every SQL command execution allocates a new in-memory DB per request (sql.NewInMemoryDB() inside Execute), committing the request path to unbounded per-request engine construction with no reuse or resource cap

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Execute` creating a new DB instance each call (`db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()`), but in this PR `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` is implemented as `return &DB{}` with no resources, and all DB methods are stubs returning `not implemented`. Additionally, `enableSqlExpressions` always returns `false`, so SQL expressions appear unreachable. The finding’s claim of “unbounded per-request engine construction” and resource risk is not verifiable from this diff (and the prior code already instantiated a new in-memory DB per execute via `duck.NewInMemoryDB()`).
